claim: For the standard five-simplex \(\Delta_5=\{x\in\mathbb R^5:x_j\ge0,\sum_{j=1}^5x_j\le1\}\), let \(F(k)=\int_{\Delta_5}e^{-2\pi i\langle k,x\rangle}\,dx\) for \(k\in\mathbb Z^5\), and let \(\Lambda(k)=\{0,k_1,\ldots,k_5\}\) be a multiset. Then \(F(k)=0\) exactly when all six nodes are distinct, or, after an integer translation normalizing the minimum to zero, \(\Lambda=\{0,0,p,p+q,p+q,p+q+r\}\) with \(qr=p(p+q+r)\), or \(\Lambda=\{0,p,p,p+q,p+q+r,p+q+r\}\) with \(pq=r(p+q+r)\), where \(p,q,r\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).

correctness.rationale: The claim follows from the exact divided-difference identity and a complete case split over all partitions of six nodes. Every repeated-node type except 2+2+1+1 is excluded by an explicit nonzero residue coefficient or formula; the remaining type reduces to the two stated necessary-and-sufficient rational gap equations. The parameterizations follow algebraically.
